subject.title: Fix spurious Claude weekly reset confetti from transient near-zero samples

question: Should Claude weekly reset detection preserve genuine usage-to-zero resets with an unchanged boundary and solve transient samples through confirmation, or redefine genuine resets to require a boundary advance?
rationale: Current main deliberately supports unchanged-boundary Claude refills, while this PR deliberately suppresses them; tests can validate either policy but cannot choose the intended user-visible contract.

options.title: Preserve unchanged-boundary resets
options.body: Rework this PR around consecutive-sample or sample-quality confirmation so false first celebrations are suppressed without invalidating current Claude refill semantics.

options.title: Require boundary advancement
options.body: Adopt this branch's stricter rule, update the merged recovery tests and migration behavior, and provide upgrade proof that legitimate Claude resets are not lost.

options.title: Close this branch
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open for a fresh fix if the current branch is no longer a useful base after the overlapping merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve unchanged-boundary resets
recommendation.body: Rework this PR around consecutive-sample or sample-quality confirmation so false first celebrations are suppressed without invalidating current Claude refill semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level choice about the intended Claude reset contract rather than a mechanical correctness question.
